title: VPC live-swap: primed-cache + health-quorum zero-downtime data-plane upgrade
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a zero-downtime upgrade pattern for Private (VPC) data plane/runtime rollouts. The approach introduces a live-swap path that combines: (1) pre-warming/priming of KV/prefix caches and model weights on target pods, (2) a health-quorum gate for each target node before traffic is routed, and (3) a reversible switching strategy in the control plane to enable fast automatic rollback.

Goals:
1) Upgrade customer VPC runtimes without increasing observed tail latency or error rate above agreed SLOs.
2) Ensure rollbacks can complete within 3 minutes to a previously healthy revision in case of regressions.
3) Make the rollout plan compatible with Terraform-managed Private stacks (IaC) and the on-prem operator.

What we will deliver in this ticket:
- A new rollout orchestration playbook (codified in the operator) that performs node-level pre-warm, health-quorum checks, traffic handover, and reversible metadata updates.
- Terraform module changes to expose the new IAM/ACL hooks and additional readiness probes as configurable parameters for customer templates.
- Health and observability additions: new metrics and alerts for KV priming coverage, per-node readiness quorum, and rollback triggers.
- Integration tests in the private-deploy harness that simulate warm-up/rollback scenarios.

Design notes / approach:
- Pre-warm strategy: control plane will create target pods in 'standby' mode. Each standby pod will: pull model artifacts, allocate KV cache reservations, and run a small synthetic prompt workload to populate common prefixes. We will maintain a priming coverage metric (percent of common prefixes hit) returned by the runtime.
- Health quorum: each target pod must pass three independent checks before added to live traffic: (A) liveness + readiness probes (kube-style), (B) KV cache priming threshold (>= configurable percent), (C) end-to-end smoke inference latency under threshold for a set of golden prompts. The rollout only advances when a configurable quorum of nodes in the new revision reports all three checks green for N consecutive intervals.
- Routing swap: rather than shifting traffic at the service level instantly, the control plane updates routing policies in an incremental fashion: it updates a per-tenant routing table to route a small fraction of new connections to new instances, increases the fraction while monitoring signals, then expands to 100%. Connections are sticky at the session granularity to avoid mid-stream model switches.
- Rollback: we keep the previous revision warmed and ready until the new revision reaches steady state. If error thresholds are breached (p95 latency spike, error rate, KV miss surge), the operator triggers an immediate traffic reversion to the prior revision and initiates a controlled drain of the new pods. A fast rollback path restores previous routing tables and, if necessary, re-primes caches on the old revision from snapshot artifacts.
- Terraform/IaC: add a flag to the Private module ("enable_live_swap_rollout") and expose tuning knobs: priming_time_seconds, priming_coverage_pct, quorum_size, smoke_test_prompts (reference to S3/drive), and rollback_thresholds. Default values are safe-conservative.

Acceptance criteria (measurable):
- Automated rollout on a test VPC completes a full revision swap (10 nodes) without customer-facing 5xx errors and with p95 latency increase <= 10% vs baseline.
- Rollback path completes in <= 3 minutes when a simulated regression (introduced in canary prompts) is observed.
- Terraform module added with schema and default values, validated by Terraform plan/apply integration tests.
- Operator exposes metrics: runtime.priming_coverage, rollout.quorum_passed, rollout.rollback_triggered (these show up in the console dashboard).
- Playbook and runbook updated in Confluence with step-by-step operator run and manual rollback guidance.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Merge IaC and operator changes behind feature flag. Deploy operator to staging.
2) Run controlled integration test: create Private stack via Terraform with feature flag enabled in an isolated VPC.
3) Execute synthetic rollout: deploy new revision with small traffic ratio. Observe priming and health-quorum metrics.
4) Gradually increase traffic while monitoring smoke tests and golden prompt diffs.
5) Promote to canary tenants (low-impact customers) for 48h.
6) Ramp to full fleet if no regressions; otherwise trigger automated rollback.

Testing strategy:
- Unit: operator state machine transitions, Terraform schema validation.
- Integration: private-deploy harness simulating KV cache warm-up, synthetic prompt workloads to assert priming coverage and smoke latency.
- Chaos: node kill and network partition tests to ensure graceful drain and reconvergence.
- Load: p99/p95 latency curves under steady-state and during rollouts.

Monitoring & alerts (initial):
- Alert if rollout.rollback_triggered > 0 (pager).
- Alert if runtime.priming_coverage < configured threshold after priming_time_seconds (ops ticket).
- Alert if per-tenant 5xx rate increases > X% during rollout.

Implementation notes and trade-offs considered:
- We considered a pure blue-green approach but rejected it due to memory and GPU footprint doubling during upgrades for large private fleets. Live-swap with standing standby pods reduces peak capacity needs.
- Prefilling caches requires synthetic prompts; maintaining a small list of golden prefixes per-customer reduces priming time but increases operational complexity. We ship with a conservative global prefix set then iterate to per-tenant tuning later.
- We defer stateful checkpoint migrations (e.g., persistent KV re-layout) until after steady rollouts; initial rollout assumes cache can be rebuilt on target nodes.

- Terraform module RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/infra/pages/PRIME-007-Live+Swap
- Integration test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-harness/tree/feature/priming

Open questions / blockers:
- We need final sign-off from Security on synthetic prompt handling and any telemetry emitted during priming (PII risk). (security review required).
- Need a small sample of customer golden prefixes from Solutions to improve priming effectiveness.

Next steps (short-term):
- Finish operator PR and unit tests (owner: Luca).
- Add Terraform schema and publish example template for customers (owner: Infra IaC).
- Create dashboard panels and set initial alert thresholds (owner: Observability).

Notes on follow-ups (future tickets):
- Per-tenant priming profiles and automated golden set extraction.
- Disk-backed cache snapshot/restore to speed rollback in larger fleets.
- Auto-tuning of priming_coverage_pct based on historical traffic patterns.
